entries.summary: @byok-sdk/protocol and @byok-sdk/core remove unused public declarations and entry exports, including constants and sealed-payload subpaths. Remove imports of these names; use retained public contracts and operations instead. Implementations needed by live schemas remain internal, accepted wire values and capability token bytes stay the same, and symbols imported by another workspace package remain public. Retained exports also record the declaration-digest changes caused by their support types becoming internal; those root declarations and runtime behavior are unchanged.

The keys and bot-collaboration Host APIs remove compatibility migrators, unused helpers, the TruthStore provider adapter and its PROVIDER_TRUTH_INVALID error code, and local Host switch import. Remove their calls and use a supported provider store; local Host export remains available.
The hosted bot-collaboration example refuses an older entity kind constraint with hosted_schema_unsupported_old before DDL; preserve the old store and provision a separate current store.

@byok-sdk/keys SqliteProviderProfileStore and inspectProviderProfileStore refuse an earlier provider-kind schema with PROVIDER_STORE_SCHEMA_STALE instead of offering migration; preserve the old store and explicitly configure a separate current store.

@byok-sdk/bot-collaboration Host opening, direct ledger writes and inspectLedger refuse local would-do rows lacking turnId with would_do_unsupported_old. Preserve the old ledger and use a separate current ledger.

The hosted bot-collaboration example refuses would-do rows held in an old scope frame with would_do_unsupported_old rather than relocating them; preserve the old hosted store and provision separately.

The hosted bot-collaboration example refuses would-do entity rows without turnId with would_do_unsupported_old rather than backfilling or archiving them; preserve the old hosted store and provision separately.

@byok-sdk/core/sqlite-node is a new entry, whose functions need Node, exporting readSqliteFileUnchanged(path, readMetadata). It opens an existing, non-empty SQLite file read-only and immutable, runs readMetadata on its main file and closes it, so a store can decide its format before any writable open, pragma or DDL; it returns undefined for :memory:, a missing path or a zero-length file, and throws SqliteReadOnlyOpenError when the file exists but cannot be stat'ed or opened read-only. sqliteOpenPath(path) and sqliteFileUri(path) name a store file for SQLite under one rule, with the Windows extended-length prefix past MAX_PATH; the client journal's writable open uses sqliteOpenPath, and the read-only check opens sqliteFileUri. SQLITE_USER_OBJECT is the SQL condition on a sqlite_schema name that excludes only the literal sqlite_ prefix; name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%' also hides user objects named sqliteX..., because _ matches any character in LIKE. The core root does not export it. No Host action is required.

@byok-sdk/client decides the format of an existing durable replica and replica lock file before any write. A durable replica in a pi-durable schema version other than the pinned one is refused with DurableReplicaFormatError instead of migrated forward, and a replica lock path that holds another database, such as the replica of a task whose id ends in .sqlite.lock, is refused instead of written. Both files stay unchanged. Released replicas are already current; preserve a refused replica and resolve it before starting this build.

@byok-sdk/client SqliteLocalTaskJournal decides an existing journal's format on its unchanged main file before the writable open and its auto_vacuum and WAL pragmas. A journal is current only when its tables and columns are exactly this build's; any other, including one that still holds the retired local_artifact_ref, local_cleanup_candidate or local_storage_usage table, is refused with JournalUnavailableError, left unchanged and no longer moved to quarantine. Startup no longer drops those tables. A journal the read-only check cannot open is refused with JournalUnavailableError and left in place rather than quarantined; a file SQLite cannot read is still quarantined. Released journals are already current; preserve or export a refused journal and resolve it before starting this build.

@byok-sdk/server/execution-core HostLedger records its format in a host_store_format table, one row per layer (k4, and k8 for Bot collaboration ledgers), and decides an existing ledger's format on its unchanged main file before the writable open, pragmas or DDL. A ledger written by 0.43.0 or earlier has tables but no host_store_format and is refused with HostStoreFormatError (code host_store_format_unsupported); it is not migrated, repaired or deleted. Finish or abandon in-flight Bot collaboration work before upgrading, then open a new ledger file at a new path.

@byok-sdk/server/execution-core: HostLedgerOptions gains expectedFormats, HostLedger exposes formats, and HostStoreFormatError is new. LedgerState loses its version field, and LedgerDump moves to version 2, so a switch dump written by an earlier release is refused. @byok-sdk/bot-collaboration: open every Bot ledger with the new botLedgerOptions (compactVeto plus the k8 format) instead of { compactVeto: botCompactVeto }; BotCollaboration refuses a ledger opened without it. CollaborationState loses its version field and SWITCH_EXPORT_VERSION is 2, so an earlier switch export is refused.

@byok-sdk/keys SqliteProviderProfileStore decides an existing store's format on its unchanged main file before the writable open, journal_mode or DDL. A store that has provider_profile but lacks a custody table is refused with PROVIDER_STORE_SCHEMA_STALE instead of having the table created, and a store the read-only check cannot open is refused with PROVIDER_STORE_UNAVAILABLE. Every released store is still accepted; preserve a refused store and resolve it before starting this build.

The hosted bot-collaboration example's Postgres store moves to STORE_VERSION 3 because the collaboration state no longer carries a version field; a scope written by version 2 is refused at open with HostedStoreVersionError, under the scope lock and before any write, and the schedulers skip it. Finish or abandon in-flight collaboration work before upgrading, then provision a new hosted store.

DaemonConfig.runtimes.pi.agentSkillPaths and PiRuntimeConfig.agentSkillPaths, default [], project to PiAdapterOptions.agentSkillPaths, so createDaemon and createRuntimeAdapters hand Pi the Host's skill files or directories without a hand-built PiAdapter. Config check refuses a relative, duplicated or NUL-carrying path, and a non-empty list with runtimes.pi.durableLane, as DaemonConfigInvalidError at runtimes.pi.agentSkillPaths. A skill path that is missing or unreadable when an Agent task starts now fails the start before Pi spawns as a non-retryable RuntimeExecutionFailure, for an embedded PiAdapter too; it used to surface as a retryable runtime_exited start failure. No Host action is required.

@byok-sdk/cloud-dataplane createPostgresCloudStores() devices.revoke() and machine supersession through devices.register() or pairing.redeemAndRegister() no longer delete the device's device_assertion_replay rows; the rows stay until the assertion expires and collectExpired removes them. A device or task assertion spent before the retirement is now refused when the same deviceId registers again with the same key. Hosts that implement their own @byok-sdk/cloud DeviceDirectory must likewise leave replay entries to expiry; no schema change or migration is needed.

@byok-sdk/bot-collaboration inboundDispositions() and inbound: projections now report answered when any round seat succeeded or delivered, even if a sibling was cancelled. Without success, cancelled seats mean failed, including when all seats were cancelled; only an authoritative root Turn can report cancelled. Update Host disposition consumers to distinguish root cancellation from seat failure; existing ledger rows use the new precedence on read.

@byok-sdk/bot-collaboration inboundKey(message) now includes conversation.kind, separating direct and group chats with the same id. All inbound and receive command identities change, so in-flight events can be admitted again once across an upgrade. Drain inbound delivery before upgrading or account for that redelivery, and use the new keys in Host comparisons and storage.

@byok-sdk/client Codex and agy starts whose runtime keeps a model other than the requested one now fail non-retryable (OAR ModelConfirmationError): task.fail carries retryable: false and failure.class 'unknown', and an embedding Host sees RuntimeExecutionFailure retry 'non-retryable', where earlier releases reported retryable. The reason text is unchanged. Do not retry these starts as transient; change the requested model or the runtime's model access, then send a new task. dsh, Grok and OpenCode are unchanged.

@byok-sdk/client agy starts that request a model may now wait up to the 30 s request deadline (packages/client/vendor/oar/552a4f9/runtimes/antigravity/session.ts:42) before failing a model mismatch; a matching update still confirms the switch immediately. A conflicting config_option_update followed by the requested model now starts the task instead of failing, and a real mismatch reaches task.fail about 30 s after the switch instead of immediately. A Host start timeout shorter than 30 s now fires first and never receives the ModelConfirmationError failure; allow at least the 30 s deadline for agy starts that request a model.

@byok-sdk/client/adapters ClaudeAdapter session followUp() no longer rejects with retryable RuntimeExecutionFailure 'claude follow-up instruction transport failed' when the write of a queued follow-up fails after Claude's own turn ended: followUp() resolves and the session's events iteration throws the retryable process failure instead. Only Hosts that embed ClaudeAdapter directly are affected; the daemon does not call followUp(). Treat a resolved followUp() as accepted, not written, and on an events failure resend the follow-up on a new session.

@byok-sdk/client Pi tasks on the pi-rpc lane send their first prompt with streamingBehavior 'followUp' and end a turn only when the run their own prompt joined settles. A task that starts while a Pi extension's own run is active (a user extension under the default agentUserContext 'inherit', a workspace .pi extension, or agentExtensionPaths) no longer fails non-retryable with 'Agent is already processing': its input joins that run, the turn ends when that run settles, and the turn's events carry the rest of that run's output. Frames written before the task's prompt was accepted or between turns, such as an extension run's settlement, progress, usage and tool events, are no longer reported as the task's events and no longer end its turn; a tool result whose call started before the task joined the run is not reported either. Every extension_error is still reported. A first prompt Pi handles without a run (an extension command) now ends the turn at once instead of waiting for the next settlement. An extension run that is still in its agent_settled hook and starts compaction can leave the first prompt without any response; that start stays pending until the Host's own start deadline (#2300). No Host action is required; a Host that needs task output free of extension runs uses agentUserContext 'excluded' and lists only Host-owned agentExtensionPaths.
@byok-sdk/client removes AgentSessionHandoffStore.getTaskTerminal(). Remove reads; recordTaskTerminal() still persists failure evidence and returns its write receipt.

@byok-sdk/client removes LocalTeamWorkspace/LocalTeamWorkspaceService.getWorkspace(), updateWorkspace() and validateMemberLease(). Use listWorkspaces() for definitions and message operations for lease validation; create a separately named workspace for a different definition.

@byok-sdk/client removes AgentEgressController.dropReceipts(), its buffer and AgentEgressDropReceipt. Call noteTransportDrop() with only the reason. Read status() for lane counters and the last reason; retain any per-drop audit history at the Host transport boundary.

@byok-sdk/client removes openDaemonLog() and DaemonLog. Embedding Hosts that write individual log lines must own their sink and rotation; daemon-wide stdout/stderr routing is not a standalone line-writer replacement.

@byok-sdk/client removes serviceExitDisposition() and ServiceExitDisposition. Use EXIT_CODE_CONTRACT for documented statuses and configure stop-on-zero/restart-on-failure in the Host supervisor; generated SDK service units already enforce that policy.

@byok-sdk/client removes PiRpcClient.waitClosed() from its declaration closure. Observe the owned child close event via an injected spawnFn for passive closure; dispose() initiates process-tree cleanup and is not a passive wait.

@byok-sdk/bot-collaboration publishes a blocked Turn as blocked:<turnId>:<code>:<fingerprint> instead of blocked:<turnId>, with value { owner, turnId, code, reason }. code is unavailable_model, schema_over_budget or current_request_too_large; reason keeps the full details; the fingerprint is the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of { code, reason }. A Turn whose reason changes while it stays blocked gets one more id per reason, and a reason that comes back republishes the same id and value. A Host that routes by the 'blocked:' prefix needs no change; a Host that builds or parses blocked:<turnId> reads turnId and code from the value instead.

@byok-sdk/server/execution-core HostOptions gains optional onSettled: a coalesced, synchronous hint after a drain cycle or memory reconciliation that settled at least one intent. @byok-sdk/bot-collaboration BotCollaboration uses it to run its own pass when K4 settles a Turn's intent in a drain the Host did not start. No Host action is required; a Host that drained BotCollaboration after terminal events or settlement projections only to advance Turns may drop those drains.

GrokAdapterOptions.agentUserContext and runtimes.grok.agentUserContext, default inherit, which changes nothing. Under excluded, a Grok Agent task runs with GROK_HOME set to an SDK-owned directory that links the user's auth.json, config.toml, trusted_folders.toml and hooks/, keeps AGENTS.md, rules/, skills, memory, plugins and the user's sessions out, keeps the Agent's sessions in <Agent home>/.byok/grok/sessions, and sets the four Claude and Cursor agents and rules variables. The start fails as a non-retryable authority failure while grok inspect still lists a user instruction file (such as an [paths] extra_rule_dirs file), when inspect fails, without a sealed Agent home, or when the user GROK_HOME has no auth.json and XAI_API_KEY is not set. A login Grok writes over the auth.json link stays in the execution scratch: the release fails with a cleanup RuntimeDisposalFailure naming its path, retention skips that execution and reports a grok_login_preserved retention-failure event with the path on every pass, and every Grok task of the daemon refuses to start until the user moves the file back to ~/.grok/auth.json or deletes it, then logs in again. The SDK never restores or deletes it. The Grok descriptor then declares isolation.userInstructions. A Bot switched from inherit cannot resume sessions it made in the user's store.

The new expiring retention class grok-session-store covers the sessions a Grok Agent task keeps under <Agent home>/.byok/grok/sessions when agentUserContext is excluded. A session folder, sessions/<encoded cwd>/<session id>/, is deleted once its newest write is older than the new DaemonConfig.storage.retention.ttlMs['grok-session-store'] (default 31 days, or the session-ledger TTL plus one day if longer; an explicit value must be at least the session-ledger TTL plus one day), unless a live session ledger still names the session or its Agent home is running a task. Grok's own index, sessions/session_search.sqlite, is never touched. A Host that switches exhaustively over retention class ids (ExpiringClassId or EXPIRING_CLASS_IDS) must add a branch for grok-session-store. No data migration: the store exists only for Grok Agent tasks under agentUserContext excluded, and resuming a pruned session fails through the existing missing-session path.

On Windows, a @byok-sdk/client Codex adapter with agentUserContext 'excluded' now refuses detection with RuntimeDetectionRefusalReason 'agent_user_context_unavailable' when the account cannot create symbolic links (Developer Mode off, non-administrator daemon). Every Codex offer on that device, Agent task or not, is then declined before claim with runtimeUnavailable.cause 'agent_user_context_unavailable' and retryable: true, in task.decline, conn.hello and the presence publish request. A Host may receive this new cause. RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE_CAUSES is append-only (@byok-sdk/protocol messages.ts): a Host must accept a cause it does not recognize; readRuntimeUnavailableCause reads it as unknown and keeps the token. The fix on the device is to turn on Developer Mode, run the daemon as an administrator, or set agentUserContext to 'inherit'.

@byok-sdk/bot-collaboration/host-kit exports supersededDeliveryIds so Host delivery adapters can identify manual-resend predecessors from resendOf and exclude them from active delivery work and retention protection.
@byok-sdk/cloud removes createInMemoryBlobs(objects, bytes). It only returned bytes.bind(objects); call objectBytes.bind(objects) on the InMemoryBlobBytes from createInMemoryBlobBytes() instead.

@byok-sdk/core PresenceStore and @byok-sdk/cloud NonceStore and InboundDedupStore gain a required deleteDevice(tenant, deviceId): Promise<void> that removes every hint, nonce or dedup ledger of that device; device retirement calls it. Hosts with a custom implementation of any of these ports add the method; the in-memory reference stores implement it.

@byok-sdk/cloud createInMemoryCloudStores takes a required presence: PresenceStore after mailbox (pass core.presence), and InMemoryDeviceDirectory takes a required third argument DeviceScopedStores { presence, nonces, dedup }, so in-memory revoke and machine supersession delete that state with the device row.

@byok-sdk/cloud DeviceDirectory.revoke and machine supersession in register must delete the retired device's presence hint, challenge nonces and inbound dedup ledgers once the registration change is durable; revoke clears that state even when no row is left, so a retry recovers a failed cleanup. Device-assertion replay entries are kept until they expire. A Host with a custom DeviceDirectory calls deleteDevice on its presence, nonce and dedup stores on both paths. ByokCloud.listPresence on the in-memory composition no longer shows a retired device until its TTL. An envelope resent after the same deviceId is registered again may be processed a second time.

@byok-sdk/cloud-dataplane PostgresPresenceStore, PostgresNonceStore and PostgresInboundDedupStore implement deleteDevice. Postgres revoke deletes the id's presence, nonce and dedup rows even when no device row is left.

@byok-sdk/protocol PROTOCOL_VERSION is 7 and there is no v6 reader: start the server side on a new store, pair the devices again, upgrade the cloud first and the daemons after. The POST /byok/messages frame (MessagesSendRequestSchema) accepts any positive v; an entry of another major is answered rejected with protocol_version_unsupported and an unknown daemon-to-server type with type_unsupported (OUTBOUND_REFUSAL_REASONS, MessageSendOutcomeSchema). A v6 daemon halts on that answer to its hello; ProtocolNegotiationError (code protocol_negotiation_failed) is the typed halt of a v7 peer refused by another major. EnvelopeSchema, MESSAGE_PAYLOAD_SCHEMAS and createEnvelope carry the v7 message set.

task.offer replaces runtime, harnessId and dispatchSelection with one required target (ExecutionTargetSchema: auto, runtime, subscription without providerId, byok, byok-profile, harness) and drops limits.maxTokens; nativeSessions needs an explicit Pi target, which targetsPi(target) tells. task.claim replaces runtime, harnessId and agentId with a required executor (ClaimedExecutorSchema); task.complete requires executor and task.fail and task.cancelled carry it after a claim. DispatchSelectionSchema and DispatchSelection are removed; the offer selection rules runtime_selection_mismatch and harness_selection_conflict are gone (OfferSelectionRule, offerSelectionViolation). @byok-sdk/cloud TaskAttempt.claimedExecutor replaces claimedRuntime and claimedHarnessId, and TaskAttemptStore.claim takes executor; AgentExecutionInputSchema and SealedAgentExecutionInputSchema embed the v7 offer. Build offers with target and read claimedExecutor; the K4 example execution core (example:host-execution-core) does both.

@byok-sdk/bot-collaboration BotOptions.dreaming.nativeSessions requests native session input only for a dream template whose target names Pi (targetsPi): a template with an auto, harness, Claude or Codex target dreams without it, where wire v6 sent the request with every runtime template. To dream with native session input, list a Pi-targeted template in dreaming.models.

Wire v7 adds the daemon-to-server task.steer_refused { steerMessageId, reason } (TaskSteerRefusedPayloadSchema, DAEMON_TO_SERVER_TYPES): a device reports a steer it received and did not deliver. reason is open (STEER_REFUSAL_REASONS, readSteerRefusalReason); the envelope id is steerRefusalEnvelopeId(steerMessageId), built on uuidFromSha256, so the first reason wins. Custom @byok-sdk/cloud compositions add the steerRefusals port (TaskSteerRefusalStore, SteerRefusalRecord; CloudStores, CLOUD_STORE_NAMES) and @byok-sdk/core MailboxStore.readMessage; both have conformance specs. Host read APIs follow in the same release.

The server advertises no capabilities in wire v7: EventsPollResponseSchema and MessagesSendResponseSchema lose capabilities, and WireAddition loses kind, rule and advertisedBy; every row is a device-gated server-to-daemon surface, and the offer's model lanes (target.lane subscription, byok, byok-profile) take the dispatch-selection row. Stop reading server capabilities.

task.decline codes are typed: DECLINE_CODES lists every known code (TaskDeclineCode), including runtime_unavailable, the offer admission codes that used to be a reason prefix, PREPARED_OFFER_DECLINE_CODES (PreparedOfferDeclineCode) and the input-preparation rejections. code stays optional and open: read it with readDeclineCode and keep unknown codes; stop parsing reason prefixes.

CAPABILITY_FLAGS loses the device flags steer and provider-profile-binding (PROVIDER_PROFILE_BINDING_CAPABILITY is removed): steering is gated on the claim's runtime capabilities, and a device that cannot bind a provider profile declines. conn.hello carries at most CONN_HELLO_CAPABILITIES_MAX_ITEMS (64) flags, and a plaintext task.steer text at most TASK_STEER_TEXT_MAX_BYTES (65,536 UTF-8 bytes); send longer follow-up input as a new task.

@byok-sdk/protocol TaskDeclinePayloadSchema now bounds task.decline reason like task.fail reason: every parse and createEnvelope redacts credentials and truncates it to TASK_FAIL_REASON_MAX_BYTES UTF-8 bytes. A Host that showed or stored the full decline reason gets the bounded text; read the meaning from code.

@byok-sdk/protocol PairRequestSchema requires expectedDeviceDigest: null, or the pairDeviceDigest (PairDeviceDigestSchema, PAIR_DEVICE_DIGEST_NAMESPACE, PairDeviceDigestInput) of the device the client knew as current for its machine. With machineId, POST /byok/pair supersedes only when it names the current device, and otherwise answers 409 PairSupersededResponseSchema (PAIRING_SUPERSEDED_CODE, currentDeviceDigest only) without consuming the code. The 401 is PairingCodeInvalidResponseSchema (PAIRING_CODE_INVALID_CODE). A v6 client gets 400; upgrade the cloud first.

@byok-sdk/protocol bounds PairRequest.deviceName and PairResponse.deviceId to 1-64 characters (PAIR_REQUEST_DEVICE_NAME_MAX_LENGTH, PAIR_RESPONSE_DEVICE_ID_MAX_LENGTH), so every field a device stores from a pairing has a bound. A server rejects a longer deviceName with 400; a client refuses a longer deviceId. deviceName, deviceId and tenantId must also be isPairingText: well-formed text with no control character (C0, DEL, C1) and no unpaired surrogate.

@byok-sdk/core tenantId() and isTenantId refuse any control character or unpaired surrogate, not only NUL, matching the protocol's isPairingText. A Host that mints such tenant ids changes them before upgrading.

@byok-sdk/cloud DeviceRegistration and PairingEnrollmentInput require expectedDeviceDigest. DeviceDirectory.register returns DeviceRegistrationResult (registered or conflict) and PairingEnrollment.redeemAndRegister returns PairingEnrollmentResult (registered, conflict, or code_invalid in place of undefined). A custom store checks the fence, supersedes and inserts in one atomic section per (tenant, product, machineId); a conflict writes nothing and consumes no code, and a consumed code with the same binding replays before the fence is read. Run the cloud conformance suite.

@byok-sdk/cloud createPairingCode (and the server's pairing.createPairingCode) refuses a productId longer than PAIRING_CODE_PRODUCT_ID_MAX_LENGTH (64) with ByokCloudError code pairing_product_id_invalid and mints nothing. The device keys its enrollment and every pairDeviceDigest by productId, so it is bounded where it enters.
createPairingCode throws ByokCloudError pairing_product_id_invalid for a productId over 64 characters and mints nothing.

@byok-sdk/client pairing rejects with PairingSupersededError (another pairing of this productId replaced this one while its request was in flight; nothing written), PairingBusyError (retryable; two pairings of one machine at once; retry with the same code) and PairingCodeRejectedError (code unknown, expired or used). FirstPairingAttemptRefusedError is renamed PairingAttemptRefusedError and has no code. PairingInputInvalidError (field deviceName or machineId) refuses an out-of-bound pairing input before anything is staged or sent. AuthResponseInvalidError's cause is optional: a malformed 2xx body carries none, since the parser's message quotes the body.

@byok-sdk/client DeviceCredentialBackend implements readPairingAttempt and savePairingAttempt (PairingAttempt) in place of the first-pairing methods; InMemoryDeviceCredentialBackend follows. clearDeviceEnrollment loses clearUnattributedAttempt and DeviceEnrollmentClearErrorCode loses pairing_attempt_unattributed: a v7 attempt always names its store. DeviceRecord drops accessToken and expiresAt, and replace always discards a staged attempt.
@byok-sdk/client AuthManager.pair, reached through BlobClient and InstallSkillPacksOptions, no longer takes the internal custody option; nothing to change unless a Host passed it.

@byok-sdk/client Daemon.pair no longer holds the productId enrollment lock across its request or its E2EE member custody; re-pairing a running daemon shuts it down outside the lock, and member entries are written only while the new enrollment holds. Hosts that relied on another store's pairing waiting for this one get the server fence instead.
@byok-sdk/client Daemon.pair stages an attempt on every pairing: the same code resumes it, a new code stages a fresh device key, except a re-pair of the store's own enrollment, which keeps its key.

@byok-sdk/client deletes a wire v6 device-enrollment OS entry, recognized by its format version without reading its key: start deletes it and reports re-pair required, pair deletes it and pairs as a first pairing, clearDeviceEnrollment deletes it. Re-pair every device after the cloud upgrade.
@byok-sdk/client pairing and token renewal errors carry only the HTTP status, never the server's response text; read the typed errors instead of parsing messages.

@byok-sdk/client no longer persists the access token: the daemon exchanges one with the device key on its first request after start and after a 401, and keeps it in memory. A start costs one /byok/challenge and /byok/token round trip; renewal writes nothing to the OS entry.

@byok-sdk/server follows the wire v7 execution target. DispatchInput (AgentResumeDispatchInput) takes one required target: ExecutionTarget in place of runtime, harnessId and dispatchSelection; pass { lane: 'auto' } for the device's own runtime preference. TaskSnapshot and the task.state ByokServerEvent expose claimedExecutor (a runtime or a harness) in place of claimedRuntime and claimedHarnessId, and SteerRejectedError carries executor in place of runtime. An execution-core intent's fresh execution template must name a concrete target; auto is refused.

@byok-sdk/server reports steer refusals. TaskHandle.steer resolves { messageId }, the id a refusal names, and refuses text over TASK_STEER_TEXT_MAX_BYTES UTF-8 bytes with ByokCloudError coordination_input_invalid before anything is enqueued. ServerTaskEvent gains { kind: 'steer_refused', messageId, reason, at }: a task's event feed yields the refusals recorded before its terminal, and ByokServer.tasks.readSteerRefusal and listSteerRefusals (SteerRefusal) read any refusal, including one recorded after the feed ended. tasks.events cursors move from te1. to te2.; a te1. cursor is refused with cursor_unknown. Exhaustive switches over ServerTaskEvent need the new arm.

The embedded server SQLite store moves to schema version 10 for wire v7 and upgrades no older file in place: opening a version 6 to 9 file fails with SqliteSchemaError SQLITE_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED, and inspectSqliteStore reports new-path-repair. Start the v7 server on a new state path and pair the daemons again; keep the old file to export its history first. Version 10 adds the task_steer_refusal table and keeps the claimed executor in two task_attempt columns, at most one of them set.

@byok-sdk/server's SQLite store decides a file's format with @byok-sdk/core/sqlite-node readSqliteFileUnchanged before it opens the file for writing, and refuses with SqliteSchemaError while the file's bytes, WAL, SHM and directory stay unchanged: an older, newer or foreign file; a current file whose tables, indexes or triggers differ from schema 10's by name or definition (a missing or changed one is SQLITE_SCHEMA_INVALID and is no longer recreated; an unknown one is SQLITE_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED). The removed migration option is no longer checked. A new store checkpoints its metadata into the main file when it is created.

Corrects a 0.43.0 regression: @byok-sdk/client ServiceInstallation.uninstall() stops and unregisters the service while current still points at the installed payload, then removes current, then the unit and launcher, then previous, versions/, snapshots/ and the receipt, so a Windows stop program under current runs instead of every uninstall failing with service_stop_failed. A failed, refused or timed-out stop throws as is, without a retry, and removes nothing: the unit and current both stay, so the service can start again until uninstall() is retried. A unit whose removal fails after the stop stays without current, so it starts no payload (#2011). A first install that fails to activate, start or pass its health check cleans up in the same order (stop, current, unit files), so a leftover unit cannot start the payload that failed; its install_health_check_failed message now names the service registration and the service unit and launcher as separate remaining artifacts. A Windows user scope lifecycle's stop() runs the Host's stop program only while a launcher runs; with none running it writes the stop marker and returns, so an uninstall() retried after current is gone finishes. Retry uninstall() after any failure.

@byok-sdk/client and @byok-sdk/client/adapters GrokAdapter (DaemonConfig.runtimes.grok) now start every Grok agent process with GROK_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1, replacing any value of that variable in the task environment. A task under agentUserContext 'inherit' on a managed Grok install no longer runs Grok's updater: it no longer writes the agent link into the install's bin/ and no longer checks for updates. Grok the user runs still updates itself; a Host that relied on SDK tasks to keep Grok current updates it outside the tasks.

@byok-sdk/cloud ByokCloudOptions.e2eeMemberStore is removed; the E2EE member store is CloudStores.e2eeMember, so the routes and the device directory that retires it use one instance. Hosts drop the option and take the store from the composition's opt-in: createPostgresCloudStores({ ..., e2eeMember: true }), createInMemoryCloudStores(..., undefined, { e2eeMember: true }) or createInMemoryByokCloud({ e2eeMember: true }), then pass the stores as cloud.

@byok-sdk/cloud binds e2ee.member to cloud.e2eeMember: CapabilityPorts loses e2eeMemberStore and gains cloud?: Pick<CloudStores, 'e2eeMember'>. Declaring the capability without the store, or passing the store without declaring it, is still refused. Callers of capabilityDeclarationForPorts pass cloud: stores instead of e2eeMemberStore.

@byok-sdk/cloud no longer exports InMemoryE2eeMemberStore. Hosts take the in-memory store from createInMemoryCloudStores(..., undefined, { e2eeMember: true }).stores.e2eeMember or createInMemoryByokCloud({ e2eeMember: true }), whose device directory retires it.

@byok-sdk/cloud E2eeMemberStore gains a required deleteDevice(tenant, deviceId): Promise<void> that deletes the packages addressed to the device's member, its registration and both pairing MACs, and keeps the chain, epochs, keyIds, shred records, KEM floor and proof requests. Hosts with their own E2eeMemberStore implement it.

@byok-sdk/cloud device revoke and machine supersession delete the retired device's E2EE member state through CloudStores.e2eeMember once the registration change is durable, and revoke does so on every call. The Host scope read omits the retired member's packages and the member id is free for another device in every composition; Postgres revoke now deletes those rows even when no device row is left. A Host with its own DeviceDirectory and E2EE store calls deleteDevice on both paths.

CloudStores.e2eeMember and DeviceScopedStores.e2eeMember are new optional members; createInMemoryCloudStores, createInMemoryByokCloud and createPostgresCloudStores take an e2eeMember: true opt-in that builds one store for both stores and directory; PostgresE2eeMemberStore implements deleteDevice.

@byok-sdk/client removes AGENT_CONTENT_READ_CAPABILITY_WORKSPACE/_TRANSCRIPT/_ARTIFACT (use AGENT_CONTENT_READ_CAPABILITIES), TOOL_AUTHORIZATION_MODES and TOOL_FILE_ACCESS (the types remain), DaemonEventKind (use DaemonEvent['kind']), and createAgentHomeProjection with AgentHomeProjectionFunction (pass agentHome.projection: { prepare } directly).
@byok-sdk/client removes listInstalledSkillPacks(); installSkillPacks() reports what it installed and projectSkillPack() copies one pack by name.
@byok-sdk/client removes TruthMemoryClient, TruthMemoryClientError and their option, input and result types. The cloud truth routes and createStoredDeviceProofSigner() are unchanged.

@byok-sdk/client control status carries versionVerdict, versionChange and the executable inside runtimes[]; the runtimeVersionVerdicts, runtimeVersionChanges and runtimeExecutables side arrays are removed, which changes DiagnosticsSnapshot's control status type. Run status and doctor from the daemon's release.

@byok-sdk/client byok-agent status and doctor refuse a control status from an earlier daemon that still sends runtimeVersionVerdicts, runtimeVersionChanges or runtimeExecutables beside runtimes[]: status reports the live status unavailable with ControlStatusShapeUnsupportedError, and doctor reports the daemon status request failed and probes runtimes locally. Upgrade the CLI and the daemon together.

@byok-sdk/client and /adapters remove RuntimeDetectResult.advisory and RuntimeDetectionAdvisory; versionVerdict { state: 'warn' } is the one unqualified-version warning and validateRuntimeDetectResult() refuses a detect result that still carries advisory. Custom adapters return versionVerdict; Hosts read availability.versionVerdict.

@byok-sdk/client removes DaemonConfigFieldRemovedError, the removed_field issue code, DaemonConfigIssue.severity and .migration, DaemonEffectiveConfig.warnings and byok-agent config check --strict; every DaemonConfig issue is an error. The generated daemon-config.schema.json closes every object (additionalProperties: false) and declares the root $schema, so editors refuse the unknown fields the daemon refuses.

@byok-sdk/client DaemonConfig: an unknown field, including one an earlier release removed (workspaceRoot, gitWorkspace, strictAgentOnly, hostedJournal and the rest), is an unknown_field error from config files and embedded createDaemon (DaemonConfigInvalidError) instead of a warning or DaemonConfigFieldRemovedError. Delete every field byok-agent config check reports.
@byok-sdk/client adds AgentMemoryOutboxVersionUnsupportedError, the typed refusal of an Agent memory outbox state this build does not read.

@byok-sdk/client Agent memory projection refuses a .byok/agent-memory-redacted-outbox-v2.json still in the 0.32.0 version 2 state with AgentMemoryOutboxVersionUnsupportedError instead of upgrading it; the file is not rewritten or deleted. Remove or archive it to resume projection.

@byok-sdk/client bundled Pi todo extension reads only $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/rpiv-todo/config.json. When XDG_CONFIG_HOME points elsewhere and that file is absent while ~/.config/rpiv-todo/config.json exists, it throws TodoConfigLegacyLocationError naming both paths instead of reading the old file or running on defaults. Move the file under XDG_CONFIG_HOME.
@byok-sdk/client/mcp-server MCP_SERVER_MAX_FRAME_BYTES keeps its 1 MiB value and now re-exports the constant the SDK MCP client and HTTP server share.

@byok-sdk/cloud reads the v7 claim executor: InMemoryTaskAttemptStore.claim and TenantBoundTaskAttempts.claim take executor, SteerRejectedError.executor replaces runtime, and TerminalResult.executor replaces harnessId and is the attempt's claimed executor (absent when the task was never claimed); projectTerminalResult takes that claimed executor as a third argument. INBOUND_REFUSAL_REASONS renames claim_harness_mismatch to claim_executor_mismatch and terminal_harness_mismatch to terminal_executor_mismatch, removes claim_harness_and_runtime_conflict, and adds steer_refusal_id_mismatch, steer_refusal_unknown_steer and task_not_claimed. Rename the reason strings an observer matches.

@byok-sdk/cloud ByokCloud.readSteerRefusal and listSteerRefusals read a task's steer refusals by steer id or by revision; TenantStores.steerRefusals and TenantBoundMailbox.readMessage carry them, and @byok-sdk/core InMemoryMailboxStore implements readMessage.

@byok-sdk/cloud handleInboundEnvelope and POST /byok/messages hold the executor to the claim and the offer. A task.claim whose executor the offer target does not allow is rejected (claim_offer_mismatch): any executor under auto, otherwise exactly the named runtime or harness. After a claim, a task.complete, task.fail or task.cancelled whose executor differs from TaskAttempt.claimedExecutor is rejected (terminal_executor_mismatch, wire not_permitted), and so is a task.complete with no claim and an unclaimed cancel or ordinary failure that carries an executor. An unclaimed daemon_interrupted recovery may name the executor its device admitted: it must be one the offer target allows (terminal_executor_mismatch otherwise), and it records no claim or owner. Devices on v7 echo the claimed executor; nothing for the Host to change beyond the reason rename.

@byok-sdk/cloud handleInboundEnvelope and POST /byok/messages accept only task.claim, task.decline, task.cancelled and a task.fail with recovery for a task that has no claim, and only from the offered device. Every other task report before a claim (task.started, task.progress, task.artifact, task.await_approval, task.approval_resolved, task.steer_refused, task.complete, task.fail without recovery) is rejected with task_not_claimed (wire not_permitted) and changes nothing. A device that claims before it reports sees no change.

@byok-sdk/cloud ByokCloud.steerTask rejects a plaintext text over TASK_STEER_TEXT_MAX_BYTES (65,536 UTF-8 bytes) with coordination_input_invalid before it enqueues anything. Send longer follow-up input as a new task.

@byok-sdk/cloud-dataplane migration 0040_wire_v7.sql adds task_steer_refusal, the one-executor check on task and the byok_wire_epoch marker. It stops before any change on a database where any table holds a row, Host configuration included. Run the migrations on a new Postgres database, then write entitlements and retention policy, and pair the devices again.

@byok-sdk/cloud-dataplane createPostgresCloudStores checks the database's wire epoch instead of pending mailbox rows: it rejects a database whose epoch is not 7, or that has none, with PostgresStoreEpochUnsupportedError (POSTGRES_STORE_EPOCH_UNSUPPORTED). PostgresMailboxProtocolUnsupportedError and POSTGRES_MAILBOX_PROTOCOL_UNSUPPORTED are removed; match the new code.

@byok-sdk/cloud-dataplane PostgresTaskAttemptStore.claim takes executor and reads claimedExecutor; PostgresTaskSteerRefusalStore is the steerRefusals port; PostgresMailboxStore implements readMessage; TENANT_ERASURE_TABLES gains task_steer_refusal.

@byok-sdk/cloud removes exports with no caller: BoardFeedClient, BoardFeedRetryableError, BoardFeedStoppedError and the BoardFeed* types; CLOUD_PORT_INTERFACES; TRUTH_RECORD_CAPABILITY and TRUTH_INLINE_CONTENT_TYPE (use CLOUD_CAPABILITIES.truthRecords); CapabilitiesResponseSchema and CapabilitiesResponse (use CapabilityDeclarationSchema and CapabilityDeclaration from @byok-sdk/core); receiptRetentionClass; InMemoryAgentMemoryProjectionStore and InMemoryAgentMemoryProjectionAuthorizer.

@byok-sdk/cloud removes createAuthPlane and its AuthPlane, AuthPlaneDeps, MintedAccessToken and PairInput types. createCloud composes the auth plane; ByokCloud.createPairingCode is the only way to mint a pairing code and enforces PAIRING_CODE_PRODUCT_ID_MAX_LENGTH.

@byok-sdk/cloud ByokCloud removes completeAgentHomeProjection and completeInputPreparation (the device completion routes still complete both), listBoardItems and acceptBoardItem (use the tenant board store), enqueueSealedAgentOffer and enqueueSealedAgentEgressOffer with SealedAgentDispatchInput and SealedAgentEgressDispatchInput (submitSealedAgentExecution is the hosted sealed lane), and enqueueProviderProvisioningNotice with ProviderProvisioningNoticeInput. ByokCloud also gains readSteerRefusal and listSteerRefusals (wire-v7-cloud-steer-refusal-reads).

@byok-sdk/cloud ApprovalObservationSchema, ApprovalTimelineEventSchema and PendingApproval require approvalId on approval_requested, a local approval_resolved and a host approve or reject. Every producer already sets it: the wire payloads require it and host decisions copy the pending request's id.

@byok-sdk/cloud approval timeline stores (in-memory, Postgres, SQLite) refuse to read or append an observation without approvalId instead of folding it as the single outstanding request; ByokCloud.approve and reject no longer refuse a pre-v4 unnamed request specially. No id is synthesized. Wire v7 starts on new stores, so a v7 store holds none.

@byok-sdk/cloud taskArchiveInput requires agentRef. @byok-sdk/cloud-dataplane removes retireAgentlessTasks, RetireAgentlessTasksOptions and RetireAgentlessTasksResult: wire v7 starts on a new database, so no pre-0039 agentless row exists. The retired-id fence stays: a task id in task_agentless_retired refuses a new offer with agent_task_already_exists.
@byok-sdk/cloud CLOUD_ERROR_CODES removes task_attempt_agent_ref_missing. Migration 0039 makes the task Agent columns NOT NULL, so the read that raised it cannot fail; drop any match on the code.

@byok-sdk/cloud-dataplane removes the resident Postgres wakes (createPostgresMailboxWake, createPostgresTaskEventsWake, MailboxWakeProbeMissedError, TaskEventsWakeProbeMissedError and their types; use the cloud's in-process wake with fallbackMs; the SQL triggers stay) and the composition factories createPostgresCloudMaintenance, createPostgresTenantErasure, createPostgresTaskRedactionStore and createPostgresAgentMemoryProjectionStore with their option types (construct PostgresCloudCleanup, PostgresTenantErasure, PostgresTaskRedactionStore or PostgresAgentMemoryProjectionStore).

@byok-sdk/cloud-dataplane removes PostgresRetentionPolicyStore, TenantRetentionPolicy and TenantRetentionPolicyInput. The tenant_retention_policy table and runMaintenance are unchanged: the Host writes and reads the policy with SQL and passes it to maintenance.

@byok-sdk/cloud-dataplane maps every outbox row through one projection (PostgresMailboxStore reads, task cancellation and PostgresCloudCleanup dead-letter pages and replay), and it brands the row's tenant with @byok-sdk/core tenantId(). A stored row whose tenant_id is not a valid tenant id now fails that read with ByokCoreError tenant_id_invalid instead of being passed through unchecked. Rows the SDK wrote always carry a valid tenant id.

@byok-sdk/client DAEMON_HALT_REASONS adds protocol_negotiation_failed, and DaemonLifecycle's halted phase carries httpStatus for it. The daemon halts instead of reconnecting when its lone conn.hello is refused as another wire major: a rejected outcome with protocol_version_unsupported (httpStatus 200) or a 4xx other than 401, 403, 409, 413 and 429. whenOpen() rejects with a DaemonHaltError whose cause is a ProtocolNegotiationError. Handle the new halt reason wherever halts are switched on.

@byok-sdk/client RuntimeTaskInput takes the offer's required target in place of runtime, harnessId and dispatchSelection, and RuntimeOperationManifest.modelTarget (the model-lane target) replaces dispatchSelection. taskRuntimeTarget returns { lane: 'runtime', runtimeId } or { lane: 'harness', harnessId }: use it as the offer target. Custom adapters read the model selection from manifest.modelTarget.

@byok-sdk/client declines carry the decline code only in task.decline code; reason is the detail alone and no longer starts with '<code>: ' (for example offer_capability_missing and the offer selection rules). Hosts that parsed a code out of reason read code instead.

@byok-sdk/client checks the offer selection rules before native-sessions support, so an offer that breaks a rule declines with the rule's code (for example native_sessions_selection_invalid for nativeSessions without an explicit Pi target) even on a device without native sessions; native_sessions_unsupported answers only an offer the rules accept.

@byok-sdk/client createDaemon starts a task's runtime and sends task.started only after the cloud accepts its task.claim; a refused claim declines the task (retryable false, reason 'claim refused: <refusal reason>', no code) and an unsettled claim fails at the offer's startup deadline. Hosts that treated task.started as the claim result read the decline instead.
